extracted.intended_audience: startup founders and early-stage startup teams
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for founders on when to hire PR firms, DIY PR tactics, how to craft funding announcements and pitches, and long-term media relationship building specifically for startups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most founders waste money on PR firms too early
rubrics_metrics.description: Most founders waste money on PR firms too early
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied recommendation: delay hiring an agency until you have sufficient traction or specific needs; do DIY PR beforehand. See 'When to Hire a PR Firm' thresholds for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best PR comes from substantive achievements, not announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Best PR comes from substantive achievements, not announcements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on real product progress, customer traction, data and use cases rather than promotional press-release-style announcements that lack substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build relationships before you need them
rubrics_metrics.description: Build relationships before you need them
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time cultivating reporter relationships in calm moments so they know and trust you when you have news. Long-term relationship building activities listed elsewhere (e.g., send relevant articles, be a useful source).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporters remember founders who didn't bullshit them
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters remember founders who didn't bullshit them
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest and straightforward with reporters; avoid fluff or promotional spin that damages credibility and future coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term reputation > short-term coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term reputation > short-term coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize building a durable reputation over chasing one-off hits; quality and honesty compound over time and are more valuable than transient coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to hire a PR firm
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations in which hiring an agency makes sense
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hire a PR firm when multiple conditions are met: $5M+ ARR; multiple ongoing news streams; the founder no longer has time for media; strategic positioning around major moments; preparing for an IPO or acquisition. These are practical thresholds rather than rules—use them to decide between DIY and agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: DIY PR tactics (do before hiring an agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions founders should take themselves before engaging a PR firm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build your reporter list manually; use HARO to become a quoted source; write thoughtful blog posts (not press releases); tweet substantively in your space; speak at conferences and panels. The emphasis is on personally building credibility and relationships rather than delegating early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcement: lead with product/what you're building
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead with what you're building, not the dollar amount
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When announcing funding, focus the lead on the product, technology, or business progress rather than the amount raised. Explain specific use of funds (e.g., hiring engineers in X, expansion to Y) to make the story substantive and newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcement: specific use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific use of funds (engineers in X, expansion to Y)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail concrete plans for the capital to demonstrate traction and purpose—this gives reporters and readers a clear signal of priorities and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcement: substantive investor quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive quote from lead investor (reasoning, not cheerleading)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an investor quote that explains why the business is compelling or strategic, not a generic promotional endorsement. Quotes should provide insight or rationale useful to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcement: customer proof points
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer logo or quote as proof point
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide customer logos, case studies, or customer quotes to validate claims and give reporters tangible evidence of market traction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcement: spokesperson available
rubrics_metrics.description: Spokesperson available for follow-up
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a knowledgeable spokesperson (founder or exec) is available and responsive for interviews and follow-ups to enable deeper reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcement: embargoed exclusive to top trade publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoed exclusive to top trade publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For important funding news, consider offering an embargoed exclusive to a top trade outlet to secure substantive, contextual coverage rather than broad wire distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcement anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Things that make a funding announcement ineffective or harmful
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid headlines that are only 'Company Raises $X'; don't use 'We're excited' CEO quotes; avoid investor quotes that are promotional fluff; don't announce with no customer or use-case validation; avoid wire-blasting to 5,000 contacts; ensure founder is available for interviews. These are common mistakes that reduce credibility and pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: The pitch template / personalized pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise, personalized email pitch structure that works
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template: Reference a reporter's recent piece, state specific news, explain the interesting angle relevant to their beat, offer a 15-minute call, have data and customer references ready, include phone number and founder name. Key criteria: personalization, relevance to reporter's beat, specificity, and readiness to provide evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term relationship building tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cultivate useful, lasting media relationships
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be a useful source on stories you're not in; send relevant articles to reporters even when not pitching; remember things they care about; don't take 'no' personally; recommend other sources when you're not the right fit. These behaviors build trust and reciprocity over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: DIY before agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: DIY before agency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer doing PR yourself in early stages—founders should build relationships and do the media work until they cross thresholds (e.g., $5M+ ARR) that justify agency costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive, not promotional
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Substantive, not promotional
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR should emphasize substance—actual product progress, customer traction, data—rather than promotional language or fluff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real news worth telling
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Real news worth telling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only pitch or announce things that represent meaningful developments; news should be interesting and valuable to readers, not filler announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Personalized pitch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches must be tailored to the reporter and their beat—reference prior work, explain why the story matters to their audience, and avoid mass-blasted generic emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Founder voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should reflect an authentic founder voice rather than corporate-speak or hollow PR-speak; authenticity builds credibility with reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term relationship building (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Long-term relationship building
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize ongoing relationship activities (helping reporters, sharing relevant info) as part of PR quality, rather than one-off outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Honest framing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame news and quotes honestly—avoid exaggeration, spin, or misleading claims; honesty preserves reputation and reporter trust.
